Hi Sam — quick back-of-envelope based on the numbers you shared.

Notes/assumptions:
- Peak baseline: 200 QPS sustained over 3 hours/day; normal hours 60 QPS; peak flash to 600 QPS for ~20 minutes during launches.
- Average request 1.5k tokens (we'll separate input/output in the model once you confirm).
- Hosted per-token: good for variable usage; no infra commitment; higher unit cost but you pay only for what you use.
- Dedicated reserved: lower unit cost at scale, predictable monthly spend (commit to N GPUs or concurrency units), better isolation and predictable tail latency.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: highest up-front cost (infra + setup + ops), lowest marginal per-token but requires customer ops and longer procurement.

Back-of-envelope numbers (very rough):
- Hosted: ~$0.0008 per token-equivalent (example) -> at 1.5k tokens/request, 200 QPS sustained -> ~864M tokens/month -> ~$691k/mo.
- Dedicated reserved (monthly commit): equivalent unit ~$0.00035 -> same usage -> ~$302k/mo; plus modest reserved capacity buffer for bursts (20% burst pool).
- Private (one-time + ops): first-year blended cost ~ $250k-$350k/mo (includes amortized infra + ops/licensing) depending on node sizing and quantization profiles.

Breakeven: around sustained high-usage scenarios (roughly when monthly token counts > ~300M) Dedicated reserved becomes cheaper than Hosted. Private becomes competitive only if you can commit to multi-year high utilization and manage ops.

Failover: yes — Redwood Dedicated supports smart routing/fallback. We can define a policy that routes overflow to Hosted (with configurable burst pool and cost caps) to handle spikes. That keeps apps online while controlling spend.

If you can confirm precise monthly token counts (or upload the filled spreadsheet), I can produce a modeled sheet with three-year TCO and a couple of commit tiers (1x, 2x, 5x reserved).

Happy to lock a 30-minute follow-up: Thurs 8/20 10:00am PT / Fri 8/21 9:00am PT — what works?
